_comment: #620 S1 D6 / A6 — the single truth table for the Cache Report four-state
One file, two readers. A duplicated vector list would be two truths, not
a parity test: each side would keep passing against its own copy while
the two algorithms drifted apart. Python and TypeScript remain two
implementations — one literal classifier is not possible across the
language boundary without code generation — so what is asserted is that
they agree on every vector, not that they share code.
`predicates` is the set the PROVIDER can evaluate at all. Claude can run
both; Codex can only ever run cache_drop, so a Codex row carrying
cache_drop alone is FULLY unevaluated rather than partial. Not applicable

vectors.name: claude-clean
vectors.why: nothing unevaluated and nothing triggered is the ordinary state

vectors.name: claude-triggered-wins-over-partial
vectors.why: triggered precedence: a thin-baseline cache_drop beside a real net_negative must not soften the verdict

vectors.name: claude-triggered-wins-over-fully-unevaluated
vectors.why: triggered precedence over EVERY other state, including the all-unevaluated one

vectors.name: claude-partial-one-of-two
vectors.why: some predicates ran and one did not

vectors.name: claude-partial-other-predicate
vectors.why: the partial state is not tied to which predicate was skipped

vectors.name: claude-fully-unevaluated
vectors.why: all predicates skipped: nothing was evaluated at all

vectors.name: codex-cache-drop-alone-is-fully-unevaluated
vectors.why: Codex can only ever evaluate cache_drop, so that one predicate skipped IS everything skipped; calling it partial would claim some other predicate ran

vectors.name: codex-clean
vectors.why: the same clean state on the single-predicate provider

vectors.name: codex-triggered
vectors.why: triggered precedence holds on the single-predicate provider too

vectors.name: observed-false-with-nothing-evaluated
vectors.why: the observed state travels separately from the verdict: a day with no activity is still `unevaluated` and reports observed=false

vectors.name: observed-absent-means-observed
vectors.why: an older envelope publishes no `observed` key and must read as observed

vectors.name: unevaluated-absent-means-fully-evaluated
vectors.why: an older envelope publishes no `anomaly_unevaluated` key and must read as clean, not as unevaluated
